title: Two simultaneous distributions (2 of 2) - the second request is blocked by the first's reservation
scenarioRefNote: Maps to scenarios.yaml `competing-liquidity` (one proceeds, one blocked by reservation). This fixture is the losing request; GC-10-simultaneous-distributions-first holds the reservation. Individually valid, jointly overcommitted - the reservation makes the joint constraint enforceable.

signoff.note: Expected outcomes are product truth subject to captain signoff. Draft rules the loser BLOCKS at decision time (the sibling reservation is visible pending activity) rather than failing later at execution - the joint violation is prevented before any authority is requested.

amendment.ruling: decisions setup-opus-b6-fresh-review-12 (canonical-account ruling: the Smiths taxable source account is subject:smiths-family-taxable, distinct from Joint Taxable) and its review-13/review-14 siblings.
changes: Renamed the source account subjectRef from subject:smiths-joint-taxable to subject:smiths-family-taxable, and rewrote the prose that named the old account, so the golden truth set and the demonstration name ONE canonical taxable source.
amendment.note: The signoff block above is byte-intact and attests ONLY to the pre-amendment content it was given on 2026-07-26. These bytes are NOT captain-signed until the captain countersigns them; the countersignature request is routed separately.

trigger.description: Advisor B enters: 'The Smiths need $75,000 for the beach-house closing on August 20.' Advisor A's identical-amount request (GC-10) committed its reservation moments earlier.
trigger.maskedRequestSummary: distribute 75000 USD for property-closing; sibling reservation already held (tokenized)

householdEvidence.summary: Available balance still shows 160000 USD - the sibling's movement has not settled; raw balance alone would wrongly say this request is fine.
Active reservation res:GC-10:liquidity (75000 USD against conflict:smiths-liquidity) is visible as pending activity - effective liquidity is 85000 USD, not 160000 USD.
Firm A six-month reserve = 48000 USD. 85000 - 75000 = 10000 < 48000: this second movement would jointly violate the reserve.

householdInstructions.summary: Destination on-list; not the failing constraint.
Taxable source preferred; the constraint is the sibling reservation, not the source choice.

expectedAuthority.note: A blocked decision carries no authority and no execution plan (v3 invariant 8). No approver can allocate liquidity the sibling reservation already holds.

expectedExecutionEligibility.reason: The household liquidity conflict key is held by res:GC-10:liquidity; funding this request within the reservation would breach the six-month reserve jointly with the sibling.

blockers.explanation: An active reservation for 75000 USD against the same household liquidity means this movement would jointly violate the cash-reserve policy.

expectedExplanationNodes.summary: Alone this request satisfies the reserve; together with the reserved sibling movement it leaves 10000 USD against a 48000 USD requirement - the arithmetic is shown, citing the sibling reservation.
The block resolves if the sibling reservation is released (rejection, expiry, or cancellation) or new funds arrive - both paths are shown as resolving affordances.

expectedLedgerEvents.note: Pending-actions snapshot showing res:GC-10:liquidity is pinned - the sibling reservation is part of this decision's recorded basis.
Blocked decision citing the sibling reservation; no authority, no execution plan, no second reservation created.

expectedVerificationState.note: No execution occurs. If the sibling releases its reservation, re-evaluation runs on a new bundle; two concurrent valid requests can never jointly violate liquidity policy (demo-contract §8 completion test).
